learning_outcomes.text: Identify experimental situations where random factors can affect the outcome, explain basic probability theoretical concepts and carry out probability calculations related to basic probability laws and theories.
Distinguish between different types of random variables, set up relevant probability-theoretic models for random experiments, and calculate important quantities in probability-theoretic models.
Use the limit theories to analyze some random trials.
Set up and analyze probability-theoretic models for certain types of quantities that vary randomly in time, e.g. in the form of time-discrete Markov chains.

syllabus_topics: Random experiments and probabilities: Outcome spaces, events, combinatorics, probabilities, urn models, conditional probabilities, Bayes formula and the concept of independence.
Random variables (one-dimensional): Discrete and continuous random variables, distribution function, probability function and density function.
Measures of mode, dispersion, and correlation: Expected value, variance, and standard deviation.
Probability distributions: Normal distribution, Binomial distribution, Poisson distribution, Exponential distribution, Uniform distribution, etc.
Stochastic variables (Two-dimensional): Simultaneous/marginal probability function, simultaneous/marginal density function, and the concept of independence.
Functions of random variables: Distribution derivation, distribution for sums of random variables and for maximum and minimum.
Approximations: Law of large numbers, central limit value theorem and poisson approximation.
Stochastic processes: Poisson process, discrete-time Markov chains.
